dialog.body: Public Works, storm line, this is Kevin. What's going on tonight?
Good evening. I am sorry to call so late. I know City Hall is closed already, so I am calling this storm number. It is all right?
Yeah, that's what it's here for. You're a little far away though, I'm only catching about half of it.
Ah, yes, the phone is on the speaker and it is on the other side of the table. One moment. [pause] Better now?
My name is Leila Haddad. We are at 6 Brewer Street, by the corner there.
Okay, six Brewer, Fifth Ward. Leila, H-A-D-D-A-D?

Yes, that is right. After the big storm, Friday into Saturday, our basement got water. About four inches. The dehumidifier, the shelves, the Christmas decorations, all wet. And the corner drain, the catch basin, it was full of leaves. Buried. The water had nowhere to go, so it came to us.
Okay. Let me pull it up. [pause] Yep, I see a drain backup logged yesterday afternoon, Daniel Haddad, same address.

Yes, Daniel called. And today a crew came, around lunch. They took off some leaves and a plastic bag from the top of the grate, and they left. That is all. But the drain is still not right. When I put the hose in this afternoon to test, the water just sits. So I am afraid. If it rains again, what happens to us?
Got it. So, crew on site today, cleared the grate only, still holding water at the basin. I'm writing that in.
Also, my neighbor, across the street, she told me she called too, about the same drain. Are these calls put together, or is each one separate? I do not want you to think it is a different problem.
Good question. I don't see her name on this one, but I'll add a note that a neighbor reported the same basin so whoever picks it up knows it's one location, more than one household.
Thank you. And, como se diz... who is the owner of this drain? The city or the state? Because someone told me Brewer is maybe state, and I worry everybody says it is the other one.
Brewer's a city street, so that basin should be ours. If it turned out to tie into something state-owned, we'd sort that out on our end. You wouldn't have to chase it.

Okay. Because there are old photo albums downstairs too. We moved them up on the shelf, but the shelf is wet already. Who can look under the street, inside the pipe? The top is clean, but I think the problem is down below.

Yeah, that makes sense. What I'm gonna do is flag this for a supervisor to look at, so somebody checks the line itself, not just the grate. I don't have a new crew date to give you tonight, honestly. That'll come from the supervisor. Best number to reach you?
The house phone. 401-555-0133.

Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-three-three. Okay, flagged for supervisor review, noted the crew visit, noted the neighbor. If water starts backing up again before you hear back, call this line, any hour.
Okay. I hope they come before the next rain. Thank you, Kevin. Good night.
Good night, Leila. Try to get some rest.
